newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes above resistance level vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes above resistance level vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan breached a key 8.3000 resistance level to close up at 8.2999 against the U.S. dollar on Thursday from Wednesday's 8.3005 on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market, dealers said.
They said comments on China's trade surplus by Dai Xianglong, governor of the central bank, encouraged active buying.
Dai said on Wednesday that China would post a trade surplus of more than $10 billion by the end of 1996.
Dealers said that such a surplus would encourage more dollar-selling and push the yuan higher.
The yuan opened slightly up at 8.3003 and moved around the opening level early in the session, hitting an intra-day low of 8.3006. It then rose above 8.3000, reaching a high of 8.2990.
Trading was active, with most done at 8.3000, traders said.
"There was strong buying below the main 8.30 resistance level today," said one dealer.
"But holding firm above 8.30 seems difficult due to a lack of direct pro-yuan factors," said a second dealer.
Dealers expect the yuan to consolidate around 8.30 on Friday.
The yuan ended down at 7.2995 from 7.2758 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0740 from 1.0725 against the Hong Kong dollar.
